headline: Growth beats, but a one-off charge dents GAAP profit
summary_short: CBRE reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $11.23B, up 15.5% y/y, with GAAP diluted EPS of $0.69 (-4.2% y/y) as a $168M non-cash UK fire-safety remediation reserve weighed on net income, while Core EPS rose 30% to $1.56.
summary_long: Revenue rose 15.5% y/y (14.3% local currency) to $11.23B, with all four segments growing segment operating profit more than 25%. GAAP net income fell 5.1% y/y to $204M and diluted EPS fell 4.2% to $0.69, held down by a $168M non-cash UK fire-safety remediation reserve; excluding that item, net income would have risen roughly 53%. Core EPS, which excludes that charge, rose 30% to $1.56 and Core EBITDA rose 33.5% to $836M. Net leverage was 1.60x with $4.4B of liquidity. CBRE raised full-year 2026 Core EPS guidance to $7.80-$7.90 from $7.60-$7.80.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based: Advisory revenue +18% on higher leasing and property-sales activity, Building Operations & Experience +15% led by a 68% jump in critical-infrastructure/data-center services, and Project Management +19% on infrastructure and real-estate project activity.

GAAP net income and EPS were reduced by a $168M non-cash increase to the UK development business's fire-safety remediation reserve; excluding that item, GAAP net income would have risen roughly 53% and EPS 57%.

Q1 2026 included a one-time real estate gain (~$301M, derived from six-month total $306M less Q2's $5M) that inflated Q1 operating income; Q2's q/q decline mainly reflects its absence, not weaker underlying segment profitability, which grew >25% across all four segments y/y.

Management raised full-year 2026 Core EPS guidance to $7.80-$7.90 from $7.60-$7.80 (23% growth at the new midpoint), citing balanced strength across all four segments, each growing segment operating profit more than 25%.
